name: Juniperus

project_scope.note: Start with Ashe juniper as the Central Texas anchor, then expand with eastern redcedar and other realistic local confusers.

priority: adult scale-leaf gland shape and position
study_strategy.warning: Habit and 'cedar-like' appearance are not enough. Use scale-leaf glands, cone characters and bark together.

quick_key.if: raised nearly circular/hemispheric resin gland on adult scale leaves + dark blue glaucous 6–9 mm cones
elongate/pitted gland tendency + generally smaller blue cones and red-brown bark

curation_status.visual_status: diagnostic-photo checklist ready; matched gland and cone macros pending

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: On an ADULT branchlet, find opposite, closely appressed scale leaves and inspect the tiny resin gland on a scale. Then compare ripe berrylike seed cones and shredding bark.
shared_traits: Evergreen conifers with scale-like adult leaves; juvenile shoots may bear awl-like leaves
Pollen cones and fleshy-looking seed cones are separate reproductive structures, not true flowers or berries
Bark often peels in fibrous strips; use gland and mature seed cones to split species

species_comparison_matrix.ashei: Raised, nearly circular to hemispheric, dark gland
species_comparison_matrix.virginiana: Pit-like or depressed gland near basal-central part of scale

species_comparison_matrix.ashei: Usually about 6–9 mm (existing canonical treatment also cites 6.5–9.6 mm)
Often rounded/multistemmed with gray-brown fibrous bark
species_comparison_matrix.virginiana: Often conical/single-trunked when young with reddish-brown shredding bark

overlap_cautions: Juvenile awl foliage cannot substitute for adult scale-leaf gland inspection.
Cone size and seed count overlap; inspect multiple mature cones and the resin gland together.
J. ashei var. ovata is treated within J. ashei in the canonical review; do not create a separate learner card.
Conic versus rounded crown and habitat are not definitive species characters.

local_lookalikes.name: Juniperus pinchotii
local_lookalikes.separate: Mature redberry juniper cones turn copper/reddish rather than blue-black glaucous; verify adult scale glands too.

local_lookalikes.name: Cupressus/Hesperocyparis and ornamental cypresses
local_lookalikes.separate: Check woody rather than fleshy-looking seed cones and scale-leaf arrangement; do not rely on the common name 'cedar'.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.show: gland raised versus pitted, same magnification and arrows
diameter and glaucous surface, multiple cones
seed count with overlapping range warning
awl-shaped juvenile versus appressed adult scale leaves
fibrous strips and crown, supporting only

handoffs.question: Select matched licensed resin-gland macros and mature seed-cone measurements for both canonical species; existing species galleries may supply anchors but must be checked for actual detail.
